newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar seen at 485/dlr by end '96 -Maza.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar seen at 485/dlr by end '96 -Maza.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar will close at around 485 bolivars per dollar by the end of the year from current levels of 470 bolivars per dollar, Venezuelan Central Bank director Domingo Maza Zavala.
"There'll be a tendency for the bolivar to soften towards the end of the year, until it reaches around 485 bolivars per dollar," he told quality daily El Nacional.
The year-end estimate uses an estaimted 1.5 percent per month depreciation rate, he said.

Maza also said Venezuela's increase in international reserves -- up some $4 billion from the beginning of the year -- had created inflationary pressures and that capital inflows "above a certain limit" had to be sterilised.

The Debt Rescue Fund and the Macroeconomic Stabilisation Fund would help sterilise the inflows from oil revenues, he said, but sterilisation in the foreign exchange market "would only result in bolivar appreciation," he said.
Approval of the funds is pending in congress.
